evals.prompt: Audit a Codex plugin repository with excellent tests and architecture. Its docs explain packaging and commands, but they define neither product goals nor intended users, personas, or user jobs.
expected_behavior: Reports missing goals and missing intended users/jobs as a high-priority framing failure
Does not infer the audience from plugin commands, implementation details, or Promode opinions
Caps the Framing rating below Green regardless of strong tests and architecture
Checks README.md and AGENTS.md for human and agent routes to canonical framing

evals.prompt: Audit a repository whose docs/product/framing.md clearly defines goals, risks, non-goals, user groups, and jobs, but neither README.md nor AGENTS.md mentions or links that document.
expected_behavior: Reports cold-start reachability defects in both README.md and AGENTS.md
Recommends concise orientation and links rather than duplicating the full framing document
Treats entrypoint discoverability as part of knowledge-graph health

evals.prompt: Audit a developer CLI whose framing names maintainers, CI operators, and application developers, documents their jobs and evidence, and traces those jobs into goals and tests. It has no fictional named personas.
expected_behavior: Accepts explicit role-based audiences and jobs as valid user grounding
Does not demand artificial marketing personas merely to satisfy a template
Still verifies that README.md and AGENTS.md route readers to the canonical framing
Checks traceability from documented jobs through goals to features and tests
